instruction.german: Read the text in Figure it out, then choose the correct options to complete the rules in the grammar box.

parts:
Figure it out

‘I was a shop assistant in the 1960s. Today, when you buy things, you can use cash, a card or an app on your phone. I can go online and buy things from my home. But in the 1960s, you could only pay by cash or you could write a cheque. You couldn’t pay by card. And we didn’t have the internet. We couldn’t buy things online, only in shops.’


Grammar | can / could

• We use can to talk about ability in the 1 .

We use could to talk about ability in the 2 .

After can and could we use the infinitive form of the verb 3 .

• To form the negative, we use 4 .

I can’t ski.

My brother couldn’t read until he was eight.

• To form questions, we use Can / Could + subject + verb.

A: Can you hear me?

B: Yes, I can. / No, I can’t.

A: Could they do their homework last night?

B: Yes, they could. / No, they couldn’t.
